purpose: Desvenlafaxine is used to treat depression in adults. It helps improve your mood, energy levels, sleep, and overall sense of well-being. Your doctor may also sometimes prescribe it for other conditions like anxiety or nerve pain.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate your mood. With depression, these chemicals can be out of balance. Desvenlafaxine works by keeping more of these chemicals available in your brain, which helps lift your mood and make you feel more like yourself over time.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, dizziness, dry mouth, sweating more than usual, trouble sleeping, constipation, and decreased appetite are the most common side effects. These often get better after the first few weeks as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly — always talk to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, irritability, and flu-like feelings. This medicine may increase thoughts of suicide, especially in young adults under 25, particularly when first starting it — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid taking it with other medications that boost serotonin without your doctor's approval, as this can cause a rare but serious reaction called serotonin syndrome.
typical_dosing: The usual starting and maintenance dose is 50 mg once daily, taken at the same time each day with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, cut, or chew it. Your doctor will decide if you need a different dose based on how you respond to the medication.
